Paper 2: Directed Writing and Composition — a core area of IGCSE First Language English.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 2: Directed Writing and Composition brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between transitive and intransitive verbs?
options: Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
Transitive verbs end in -ed and intransitive in -ing.
Transitive verbs take a direct object ('she ate the cake'); intransitive verbs don't ('she slept'). Some verbs are both depending on use ('she ran' / 'she ran the company').
Transitive verbs are action verbs and intransitive are linking verbs.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between descriptive and prescriptive approaches to language?
options: Descriptivists describe written language and prescriptivists describe spoken language.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
Descriptivists describe how language is actually used; prescriptivists rule on how language ought to be used — modern linguistics is descriptivist.
Register is the same as accent.
Transitive verbs end in -ed and intransitive in -ing.
Register is the same as accent.
A variety of language used in a particular social setting — varying by formality, field (topic) and mode (spoken/written) to suit audience and purpose.
Register is just how loud you speak.
